newsitem.title: ITALY: Mafia godfather's treasure trove found in Sicily.
newsitem.headline: Mafia godfather's treasure trove found in Sicily.

text.p: Police on Friday said they had unearthed a treasure trove of gold and precious jewels stashed away by the Mafia's jailed "boss of bosses" Salvatore "The Beast" Riina.
Investigators said the treasure, worth at least $1.3 million, had been hidden under the floor of an apartment in Castelvetrano, near the western Sicilian city of Trapani.

The haul included up to 40 kilos (90 lbs) of gold bars, 300 gold sovereigns, several gold watches, diamonds, blank passports and a gem-encrusted crucifix that Riina may have worn at meetings of the Mafia's ruling "commission", police said.
They were led to it by a new Mafia turncoat who told police Riina had given him the valuables to hide in 1991 or 1992.

"This man is a new collaborator. He has not only been telling us about killings and crimes but has also allowed us to hit the Mafia's economic interests," deputy prosecutor Luigi Croce told a news conference in the Sicilian capital Palermo.
He did not name the informer.
Eight people were arrested on charges of Mafia association following the four a.m. raid and 14 warrants were served on suspected Mafiosi already in jail on other charges, police said.
Riina, once the undisputed head of the Mafia, was arrested in January 1993 after 23 years on the run and is serving several life prison sentences.

Since his arrest, magistrates have confiscated numerous houses, apartments and tracts of land, mostly in Sicily, believed to have been owned by Riina but registered under names of family members or accomplices.
